shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः परमार्थवित् । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं राघवं दीप्ततेजसम् ।। 7.54.1 ।।
transliteration: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā lakṣmaṇaḥ paramārthavit | uvāca prāñjalirvākyaṃ rāghavaṃ dīptatejasam || 7.54.1 ||
translation: रामस्य of Rama, भाषितम् the speech, श्रुत्वा having heard, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, परमार्थवित् knower of the highest truth, उवाच spoke, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, वाक्यम् words, राघवम् to Rama, दीप्ततेजसम् radiant with splendor.
explanation: Having heard Rama's speech, Lakshmana, who knew the highest truth, spoke words with folded hands to Rama, who was radiant with splendor.
comments: Lakshmana asks how King Nrga met his curse -- Rama recounts that Nrga, learning the brahmins had cursed and departed, consecrated his son Vasu, had pleasant caves prepared for his long ordeal, counselled his son on a Kshatriya's duty and the might of destiny, and then entered the well to live out the curse.

shloka_text: अल्पापराधे काकुत्स्थ द्विजाभ्यां शाप ईदृशः । महान्नृगस्य राजर्षेर्यमदण्ड इवापरः ।। 7.54.2 ।।
transliteration: alpāparādhe kākutstha dvijābhyāṃ śāpa īdṛśaḥ | mahānnṛgasya rājarṣeryamadaṇḍa ivāparaḥ || 7.54.2 ||
translation: अल्पापराधे for a small offense, काकुत्स्थ O Kakutstha, द्विजाभ्याम् by the two Brahmins, शापः a curse, ईदृशः such, महान् severe, नृगस्य of Nṛga, राजर्षेः of the royal sage, यमदण्डः the punishment of Yama, इव like, अपरः another.
explanation: O Kakutstha, for a minor offense, such a severe curse was given by the two Brahmins, like another punishment from Yama for the royal sage Nṛga.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा तु पापसंयुक्तमात्मानं पुरषर्षभ । किमुवाच नृगो राजा द्विजौ क्रोधसमन्वितौ ।। 7.54.3 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā tu pāpasaṃyuktamātmānaṃ puraṣarṣabha | kimuvāca nṛgo rājā dvijau krodhasamanvitau || 7.54.3 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, तु indeed, पापसंयुक्तम् associated with sin, आत्मानम् himself, पुरषर्षभ O best of men, किम् what, उवाच did say, नृगः Nṛga, राजा king, द्विजौ to the two Brahmins, क्रोधसमन्वितौ filled with anger.
explanation: O best of men, what did King Nṛga say to the two enraged Brahmins after hearing himself accused of sin?

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु राघवः पुनरब्रवीत् । शृणु सौम्य यथा पूर्वं स राजा शापविक्षतः ।। 7.54.4 ।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇenaivamuktastu rāghavaḥ punarabravīt | śṛṇu saumya yathā pūrvaṃ sa rājā śāpavikṣataḥ || 7.54.4 ||
translation: लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, राघवः Rama, पुनः again, अब्रवीत् said, शृणु listen, सौम्य O gentle one, यथा how, पूर्वम् previously, सः that, राजा king, शापविक्षतः afflicted by the curse.
explanation: When Lakshmana thus spoke, Rama again said, "O gentle one, listen to how that king was previously afflicted by the curse."

shloka_text: अथाध्वनि गतौ विप्रौ विज्ञाय स नृगस्तदा । आहूय मन्त्रिणः सर्वान्नैगमान्सपुरोधसः ।। 7.54.5 ।।
transliteration: athādhvani gatau viprau vijñāya sa nṛgastadā | āhūya mantriṇaḥ sarvānnaigamānsapurodhasaḥ || 7.54.5 ||
translation: अथ then, अध्वनि on the way, गतौ gone, विप्रौ the two Brahmins, विज्ञाय having known, सः that, नृगः Nṛga, तदा then, आहूय having summoned, मन्त्रिणः ministers, सर्वान् all, नैगमान् citizens, सपुरोधसः along with the priests.
explanation: Then, having understood that the two Brahmins had departed, King Nṛga summoned all his ministers, citizens, and priests.

shloka_text: तानुवाच नृगो राजा सर्वाश्च प्रकृतीस्तथा । दुःखेन सुसमाविष्टः श्रूयतां मे समाहितैः ।। 7.54.6 ।।
transliteration: tānuvāca nṛgo rājā sarvāśca prakṛtīstathā | duḥkhena susamāviṣṭaḥ śrūyatāṃ me samāhitaiḥ || 7.54.6 ||
translation: तान् to them, उवाच said, नृगः Nṛga, राजा king, सर्वाः all, च and, प्रकृतीः subjects, तथा also, दुःखेन by sorrow, सुसमाविष्टः deeply afflicted, श्रूयताम् let it be heard, मे from me, समाहितैः by those who are attentive.
explanation: Deeply afflicted by sorrow, King Nṛga spoke to all of them, including his subjects, saying, "Let my words be heard by all of you with attention."

shloka_text: नारदः पर्वतश्चैव मम दत्त्वा महद्भयम् । गतौ त्रिभुवनं भद्रौ वायुभूतावनिन्दितौ ।। 7.54.7 ।।
transliteration: nāradaḥ parvataścaiva mama dattvā mahadbhayam | gatau tribhuvanaṃ bhadrau vāyubhūtāvaninditau || 7.54.7 ||
translation: नारदः Narada, पर्वतः Parvata, च and, एव indeed, मम to me, दत्त्वा having given, महत् great, भयम् fear, गतौ have gone, त्रिभुवनम् to the three worlds, भद्रौ the two noble ones, वायुभूतौ having become like wind, अनिन्दितौ the two blameless ones.
explanation: The noble and blameless Narada and Parvata, having instilled great fear in me, have indeed departed to the three worlds, swift as the wind.

shloka_text: कुमारो ऽयं वसुर्नाम स देवो ऽद्याभिषिच्यताम् । श्वभ्रं च यत्सुखस्पर्शं क्रियतां शिल्पिभिर्मम । यत्राहं सङ्क्षयिष्यामि शापं ब्राह्मणनिःसृतम् ।। 7.54.8 ।।
transliteration: kumāro 'yaṃ vasurnāma sa devo 'dyābhiṣicyatām | śvabhraṃ ca yatsukhasparśaṃ kriyatāṃ śilpibhirmama | yatrāhaṃ saṅkṣayiṣyāmi śāpaṃ brāhmaṇaniḥsṛtam || 7.54.8 ||
translation: कुमारो अयम् this boy, वसुः नाम by name Vasu, सः he, देवः god, अद्य today, अभिषिच्यताम् let him be consecrated, श्वभ्रम् a pit/cave, च and, यत् which is, सुखस्पर्शम् pleasant to touch, क्रियताम् let it be made, शिल्पिभिः by artisans, मम for me, यत्र where, अहम् I, सङ्क्षयिष्यामि will exhaust/destroy, शापम् the curse, ब्राह्मणनिःसृतम् issued from a Brahmin.
explanation: Let this boy named Vasu be consecrated as a god today, and let artisans construct for me a pleasant cave where I can exhaust the curse issued by a Brahmin.

shloka_text: वर्षघ्नमेकं श्वभ्रं तु हिमघ्नमपरं तथा । ग्रीष्मघ्नं तु सुखस्पर्शमेकं कुर्वन्तु शिल्पिनः ।। 7.54.9 ।।
transliteration: varṣaghnamekaṃ śvabhraṃ tu himaghnamaparaṃ tathā | grīṣmaghnaṃ tu sukhasparśamekaṃ kurvantu śilpinaḥ || 7.54.9 ||
translation: वर्षघ्नम् rain-proof, एकम् one, श्वभ्रम् pit/cave, तु indeed, हिमघ्नम् cold-proof, अपरम् another, तथा similarly, ग्रीष्मघ्नम् summer-proof, तु and, सुखस्पर्शम् pleasant to touch, एकम् one, कुर्वन्तु let them make, शिल्पिनः artisans.
explanation: The artisans should construct one cave that is rain-proof, another that is cold-proof, and a third, pleasant to touch, that is summer-proof.

shloka_text: फलवन्तश्च ये वृक्षाः पुष्पवत्यश्च या लताः । विरोप्यन्तां बहुविधाश्छायावन्तश्च गुल्मिनः ।। 7.54.10 ।।
transliteration: phalavantaśca ye vṛkṣāḥ puṣpavatyaśca yā latāḥ | viropyantāṃ bahuvidhāśchāyāvantaśca gulminaḥ || 7.54.10 ||
translation: फलवन्तः fruit-bearing, च and, ये which, वृक्षाः trees, पुष्पवत्यः flower-bearing, च and, या which, लताः creepers, विरोप्यन्ताम् let them be planted, बहुविधाः of many kinds, छायावन्तः shade-giving, च and, गुल्मिनः shrubs.
explanation: Let fruit-bearing trees, flowering creepers, and various kinds of shade-giving shrubs be planted.

shloka_text: क्रियतां रमणीयं च श्वभ्राणां सर्वतोदिशम् । सुखमत्र वसिष्यामि यावत्कालस्य पर्ययः ।। 7.54.11 ।।
transliteration: kriyatāṃ ramaṇīyaṃ ca śvabhrāṇāṃ sarvatodiśam | sukhamatra vasiṣyāmi yāvatkālasya paryayaḥ || 7.54.11 ||
translation: क्रियताम् let it be made, रमणीयम् beautiful, च and, श्वभ्राणाम् of the pits/caves, सर्वतोदिशम् in all directions, सुखम् comfortably, अत्र here, वसिष्यामि I will dwell, यावत् as long as, कालस्य of time, पर्ययः the change/end.
explanation: Let the surroundings of the caves be made beautiful in all directions, for I will dwell there comfortably until the end of my destined time.

shloka_text: पुष्पाणि च सुगन्धीनि क्रियतां तेषु नित्यशः । परिवार्य यथा मे स्युरध्यर्धं योजनं तथा ।। 7.54.12 ।।
transliteration: puṣpāṇi ca sugandhīni kriyatāṃ teṣu nityaśaḥ | parivārya yathā me syuradhyardhaṃ yojanaṃ tathā || 7.54.12 ||
translation: पुष्पाणि flowers, च and, सुगन्धीनि fragrant, क्रियताम् let them be placed/made, तेषु in them, नित्यशः always, परिवार्य surrounding, यथा so that, मे for me, स्युः they may be, अध्यर्धम् one and a half, योजनम् Yojana, तथा thus.
explanation: Let fragrant flowers always be placed in them, surrounding the area for me to a distance of one and a half Yojanas.

shloka_text: एवं कृत्वा विधानं स सन्दिदेश वसं तदा । धर्मनित्यः प्रजाः पुत्र क्षत्रधर्मेण पालय ।। 7.54.13 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ kṛtvā vidhānaṃ sa sandideśa vasaṃ tadā | dharmanityaḥ prajāḥ putra kṣatradharmeṇa pālaya || 7.54.13 ||
translation: एवं thus, कृत्वा having made, विधानं arrangement, स he, सन्दिदेश instructed, वसं O son, तदा then, धर्मनित्यः ever devoted to dharma, प्रजाः subjects, पुत्र O son, क्षत्रधर्मेण by the duty of a Kshatriya, पालय protect.
explanation: Having made this arrangement, the king then instructed his son, "O son, ever devoted to righteousness, protect your subjects according to the duty of a Kshatriya."

shloka_text: प्रत्यक्षं ते यथा शापो द्विजाभ्यां मयि पातितः । नरश्रेष्ठ सरोषाभ्यामपराधे ऽपि तादृशे ।। 7.54.14 ।।
transliteration: pratyakṣaṃ te yathā śāpo dvijābhyāṃ mayi pātitaḥ | naraśreṣṭha saroṣābhyāmaparādhe 'pi tādṛśe || 7.54.14 ||
translation: प्रत्यक्षं directly, ते by you, यथा how, शापो curse, द्विजाभ्यां by the two Brahmins, मयि upon me, पातितः cast, नरश्रेष्ठ O best among men, सरोषाभ्यां by the two angry ones, अपराधे in the offense, अपि even, तादृशे such.
explanation: O best among men, you yourself witnessed how a curse was inflicted upon me by the two angry Brahmins, even for such an offense.

shloka_text: मा कृथास्तनुसन्तापं मत्कृते ऽपि नरर्षभ । कृतान्तः कुशलः पुत्र येनास्मि व्यसनीकृतः ।। 7.54.15 ।।
transliteration: mā kṛthāstanusantāpaṃ matkṛte 'pi nararṣabha | kṛtāntaḥ kuśalaḥ putra yenāsmi vyasanīkṛtaḥ || 7.54.15 ||
translation: मा do not, कृथाः make, तनुसन्तापं bodily distress, मत्कृते for my sake, अपि even, नरर्षभ O best of men, कृतान्तः destiny, कुशलः powerful, पुत्र O son, येन by which, अस्मि I am, व्यसनीकृतः made miserable.
explanation: O best of men, do not grieve for my sake, O son, for destiny is powerful, and it is by its force that I have been afflicted with this misery.

shloka_text: प्राप्तव्यान्येव प्राप्नोति गन्तव्यान्येव गच्छति । लब्धव्यान्येव लभते दुःखानि च सुखानि च ।। 7.54.16 ।।
transliteration: prāptavyānyeva prāpnoti gantavyānyeva gacchati | labdhavyānyeva labhate duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca || 7.54.16 ||
translation: प्राप्तव्यान्येव only those that are to be obtained, प्राप्नोति one obtains, गन्तव्यान्येव only those that are to be gone to, गच्छति one goes, लब्धव्यान्येव only those that are to be received, लभते one receives, दुःखानि sorrows, च and, सुखानि joys, च and.
explanation: One obtains only what is destined to be obtained, goes only where one is destined to go, and receives only the sorrows and joys that are destined to be received.

shloka_text: पूर्वे जात्यन्तरे वत्स मा विषादं कुरुष्व ह ।। 7.54.17 ।।
transliteration: pūrve jātyantare vatsa mā viṣādaṃ kuruṣva ha || 7.54.17 ||
translation: पूर्वे in a former, जात्यन्तरे birth, वत्स O son, मा do not, विषादं sorrow, कुरुष्व make, ह indeed.
explanation: O son, do not grieve over what happened in a former birth.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा नृपस्तत्र सुतं राजा महायशाः । श्वभ्रं जगाम सुकृतं वासाय पुरुषर्षभ ।। 7.54.18 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā nṛpastatra sutaṃ rājā mahāyaśāḥ | śvabhraṃ jagāma sukṛtaṃ vāsāya puruṣarṣabha || 7.54.18 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, नृपः the king, तत्र there, सुतम् to his son, राजा the king, महायशाः highly renowned, श्वभ्रम् into the well, जगाम went, सुकृतम् well-made, वासाय for dwelling, पुरुषर्षभ O best among men.
explanation: O best among men, having thus spoken to his son, the highly renowned king went into the well, which was well-constructed for his dwelling.

shloka_text: एवं प्रविश्यैव नृपस्तदानीं श्वभ्रं महारत्नविभूषितं तत् । सम्पादयामास तदा महात्मा शापं द्विजाभ्यां हि रुषा विमुक्तम् ।। 7.54.19 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ praviśyaiva nṛpastadānīṃ śvabhraṃ mahāratnavibhūṣitaṃ tat | sampādayāmāsa tadā mahātmā śāpaṃ dvijābhyāṃ hi ruṣā vimuktam || 7.54.19 ||
translation: एवम् thus, प्रविश्यैव having just entered, नृपः the king, तदानीम् at that time, श्वभ्रम् into the well, महारत्नविभूषितम् adorned with great jewels, तत् that, सम्पादयामास he fulfilled, तदा then, महात्मा the great-souled one, शापम् the curse, द्विजाभ्याम् by the two Brahmins, हि indeed, रुषा with anger, विमुक्तम् uttered.
explanation: Having thus just entered that well adorned with great jewels, the great-souled king then fulfilled the curse that had indeed been uttered with anger by the two Brahmins. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 54 ।। Thus ends the fifty-fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
